note: Swappable grammar pack (R46, §9.3/§9.11) for the dedicated/bare-metal line. Machine-checked wall between namespaces: 'decision' strings appear while the player decides or loses (labels, terms, refusals, alerts, status rungs) and stay SOBER per §9.3 clauses 2-3; 'flavour' carries the recognition comedy for quiet surfaces. Authenticity law for this line (§9.3/§9.11): the drama is the OPERATOR's — the dark square in the row, the serial numbers marching, the four-hour promise against one van — never the attack tooling. No payloads, commands, tool names-as-how-to, or technique instruction anywhere; abuse exists only as complaint, upstream notice, vendor silence, and consequence.

nodeId.desc: Board object the decision surface is about (rack / server id).

availableAtTick.desc: Tick at which the queued intent or a freed hand presents.

slotName.desc: Socket designation on a node (PSU, uplink, drive bay).

serverName.desc: A dedicated box by its hand-written nameplate.

serialNumber.desc: Asset tag / RMA serial — the batch identifier the defect marches down.

rackPosition.desc: Frame position of a box in the stable row (U-slot).

utilizationPct.desc: Rack utilization — the win metric and the quiet killer (§15395).

provisioningMinutes.desc: Elapsed install time on the crash-cart screen — the signature meter's number (§1.3).

installPct.desc: Installer progress percentage the crash-cart screen creeps through.

powerState.desc: IPMI power readout for a box (on/off/cycling) — what the keyhole is allowed to see.

quoteAmount.desc: Handwritten quote figure from the sales desk (§12521).

uplinkMbps.desc: Metered rack-uplink throughput a neighbour is spending.

complaintCount.desc: Abuse-desk complaint count in a conscription tally.

victimName.desc: The target whose NOC is filing your customer's volley.

hour.desc: Clock hour a ticket or notice was filed at.

minute.desc: Clock minute a ticket or notice was filed at.

day.desc: Day of the quarter, for the intern's log.

decision.type.dedicated.name: Root Is Theirs
decision.type.dedicated.codex: The bare-metal line: one customer per box, all of it theirs, including the mess. You see traffic, power state and the IPMI console, and your whole console is email, null-route, and power-off. Rack space and provisioning time are the scarce lungs; utilization is the whole game; and gear bought together fails together, one serial number at a time.
decision.goal.dedicated.binding: An empty dedicated server is pure loss every month, and the only hands that can fill a rack are the same hands that answer for the abuse it commits.
decision.scarce.dedicated.qos: The dead box outranks the report, and nothing outranks the van already on the road — the install screen, the spares shelf and the four-hour promise are the whole queue, and every hour of provisioning you sold cheap is an hour the customer will spend loudly.
decision.skin.dedicated.inspector: The Stable and the Workshop in gunmetal and amber — a row of mismatched boxes with hand-written label-tape nameplates, asset tags on every bezel, scratches and re-drilled ears kept honest, green LED pilots breathing one box per customer, and the crash cart parked at the end of the row with its installer still running.
decision.economy.dedicated.bad-month: A hardware batch failure across gear you bought together.
decision.relations.dedicated.mastery: The shelf reads the row: spares are staged before the batch fails, not after the fifth ticket; quotes are sold against occupancy charts, not against enthusiasm; and the abuse desk answers before the upstream notice arrives.
decision.relations.dedicated.distillate: Playbook: act through the keyhole like an engineer on call — replace every unit of agency you remove with two units of visibility, price the empty rack like the fire it is, and treat every healthy green LED over an unbilled box as a number to argue with.
decision.handover.dedicated.runs-out: Your rack space and your provisioning time. Sold-out is a door you can price; a dead box on a three-hour install path is a countdown you cannot.
decision.handover.dedicated.kills-you: Capex stranded in dark rows: the batch you bought together failing apart, and utilization that never crossed breakeven while the lease depreciated underneath.
decision.handover.dedicated.customer-wants: Root, and the four-hour promise. They came for the whole box; they stay for the van that actually shows up.
decision.rosetta.dedicated.occupancy: Rack occupancy is the oversell ratio seen from the empty side: capacity already paid for and sold to nobody, depreciating in the dark.
decision.rosetta.dedicated.keyhole: The IPMI power-cycle is the triage window aimed at a machine instead of a queue — every unit of agency you remove must be replaced with two units of visibility.
decision.scenarios.dedicated.truck-roll-race: A box dies mid-volley and the promise says four hours: the spares shelf, the remote-hands retainer and the crash cart all line up at the start gun, and the customer's traffic graph watches the racetrack.
decision.scenarios.dedicated.hollow-stable: The row fills with dark squares: every nameplate billed, every pilot unlit, utilization sagging below the breakeven nobody put a number on — the quietest catastrophe in the product line, and the only one that never files a ticket.
decision.scenarios.dedicated.foothold-abuse: A customer's box falls the way boxes fall when they hold root alone, and the internet answers by address space: your ASN, their volley, your abuse desk doing its best with somebody else's mess.
decision.alert.hollow-row: {serverName} at {rackPosition}: powered, billed, and used by no one. Row utilization {utilizationPct}. Nothing is wrong. That is the alarm.
decision.alert.batch-serial: Third failure this week sharing serial lineage {serialNumber}. The RMA queue is describing a purchase order — Companion C's bought-together failure, arriving one slot at a time.
decision.alert.install-stall: Crash cart on {serverName}: {installPct}% with {provisioningMinutes} on the clock. The provisioning meter is the product meter on this line; the customer is waiting at a screen you cannot speed up with wishes.
decision.alert.power-cycle: IPMI on {serverName} reports {powerState}. The keyhole offers email, null-route, power-off. Choose loudly; observe constantly.
decision.terms.setup-fee: Quote {quoteAmount} with setup fee: month-to-month with a fee is the doc'd shape of this line (§1.12) — the fee is the deposit the empty rack takes off your fear.
decision.terms.truck-roll-sla: The four-hour replacement expectation (§1.3) is priced here as an SLA, not a favor: every leg of it — spares depth, remote hands, the van — is a buildable you can starve.
decision.terms.uplink-metered: Rack uplink at {uplinkMbps}: metered shared capacity on a single-tenant promise. The neighbour's flood bills the row, and your customer reads the graph as your apology.
decision.refusal.hands-exhausted: Both hands are committed. The {verb} intent is queued and presents when a hand frees at tick {availableAtTick}.
decision.refusal.stamped-in-future: The {verb} intent is stamped for tick {availableAtTick}, ahead of the current minute. Nothing was spent.
decision.refusal.unknown-node: No board object named {nodeId} exists at the current tick. Nothing was changed.
decision.refusal.edge-exists: A {relationKind} cable already links {nodeId} to those endpoints. The existing edge was left as it is.
decision.refusal.slot-occupied: {slotName} on {nodeId} is occupied. One supplier per socket; disconnect before you reconnect.
decision.status.rung-5: We are aware of the fire.

flavour.ticket.subject.serial-march: my box is beeping at boot again (fourth this month)
flavour.ticket.body.serial-march: Ticket {ticketId}, filed {hour}:{minute}. You know it is not one box because the RMA pile has a theme. The vendor's known-issue notice has a serial range. Your invoices do not mention serial ranges, but the depreciation schedule now has a personality.
flavour.ticket.subject.leds-mean: delivered yesterday - what do the lights mean
flavour.ticket.body.leds-mean: New box at {rackPosition}, root delivered, enthusiasm undimmed. The customer has held a server exactly once, in a photograph, and is now asking what the amber pilot wants from them. Nobody is wrong here. That is what makes it funny.
flavour.ticket.subject.graph-flat: is my server dead? the traffic line is a straight line
flavour.ticket.body.graph-flat: Power on, panel green, install log clean. The line is flat because the product the server runs launches Tuesday. You are being asked to explain success to somebody who has only ever measured it with noise.
flavour.ticket.subject.abuse-forwarded: FW: FW: FW: your network, our inbox, four hundred compliments
flavour.ticket.body.abuse-forwarded: A NOC you will never meet has forwarded {complaintCount} complaints about traffic wearing your address space. The box belongs to a customer, the kernel belongs to a customer, the consequences, per your own contract, belong to you.
flavour.abuse.canon.noc-filed: From: {victimName} NOC — a denial-of-service against their infrastructure was amplified from a server hosted by you at {uplinkMbps} sustained. They have the serial range. They are being extremely reasonable about it, which is worse.
flavour.abuse.canon.spam-listing: Listing notice: your customer's range appears on three blocklists as of this morning. Nobody on your side sent anything. The box with root did, and the mail never had your name on it until now.
flavour.abuse.canon.upstream-notice: Upstream notice: transit at the rack row will be limited until the originating host at {rackPosition} is quiet. The stable stays lit. The road out of it develops a toll booth.
flavour.press.headline.batch: {hostName} confirms fleet-wide defect in a single purchased batch; replacement timeline described as 'a function of the shelf, not the vendor'. Analysts note the word 'batch' appeared in no marketing material.
flavour.press.headline.quiet: {hostName} downtime never announced; a regional service discovered its dependency at 3 a.m. and its nameplate was, by all reports, very legible.
flavour.forum.thread.whois-routing: Anyone else's abuse complaints arrive addressed to their HOSTING ASN and not the actual bot's owner? Mine says my IP range. My IP range says my customer. My customer says they did not consent to this sentence.
flavour.forum.thread.four-hours: Warranty said four hours. The shelf said otherwise. We have started keeping a second spare per batch line like it's a hobby. It should not be a hobby.
flavour.chatter.desk.quiet: The sales desk is quiet and the utilization dial is quieter. On this line those are the same sentence.
flavour.chatter.stable.smell: New-box smell, old-box dust, and the particular silence of a rack nobody bought. The stable tells you which one you are running.
flavour.codex.keyhole: The keyhole is a design, not a limitation: traffic, power, IPMI. Everything else is the customer's, including the consequences — so the visibility you keep is engineered to be legible at Z1, where the row reads as a ledger of names.
flavour.codex.batch: Hardware bought together fails together. The doc's bad month for this line is not an attacker; it is a purchase decision arriving late, one serial number at a time.
flavour.loading.tip.visibility: Every unit of agency you remove must be replaced with two units of visibility. The crash cart screen is not a joke; it is the trade being honored.
flavour.loading.tip.empty: An empty dedicated server is pure loss every month. Sell the rack you own before you quote the one you do not.
flavour.intern.entry.ledcount: Day {day}: the row is forty nameplates deep and the boss counts lit pilots the way other lines count tickets. Nobody warned me the quiet would be the loud part.
flavour.intern.entry.labeltape: Day {day}: learned the customer's name goes on the tape by hand, at Z1, where they can read it. 'Root is theirs,' the senior tech said, 'which is exactly why the label is ours.'
flavour.sticky.note.spares: Bought the second spare BEFORE the fifth ticket. — postmortem wall, {serialNumber} incident
flavour.vendor.reply.firmware: Have you tried updating to the latest firmware?
flavour.vendor.reply.log-bundle: Please collect a full log bundle.
flavour.vendor.reply.known-issue: This is a known issue, fixed in the next release (no ETA).
flavour.achievement.four-hour-hero: Four Hours, One Van, No Excuses.
flavour.canary.row-tally: {complaintCount} notices routed at {serverName} while the row hums at {utilizationPct} — the abuse desk and the occupancy chart are the same instrument, read twice.
